drhp.business: Haldyn Glass Limited manufactures glass containers for packaging, operating in a single primary business segment viz. glass bottles / containers. It historically made predominantly flint (transparent) containers and during FY 2025-26 also commenced manufacture of coloured (amber/brown and green) glass bottles for the beer segment. Liquor continues to account for the largest share of the Company's offtake, but the portfolio now spans liquor, food & beverages, pharmaceuticals, softdrinks and toiletries, sold to customers in India and in international markets including the US.
drhp.end_markets: Alcoholic beverages / liquor (largest share of offtake)|Beer (entered during FY 2025-26)|Non-alcoholic beverages / softdrinks|Food|Pharmaceuticals|Personal care and toiletries|Homecare|India (domestic)|International markets, with an established presence and long-standing customer relationships in the US
drhp.expansion: The only expansion the FY 2025-26 annual report describes is the entry into coloured glass: having earlier made predominantly flint (transparent) containers, the Company commenced manufacturing coloured (amber/brown and green) glass bottles for the beer segment during the year and commercialised them within FY26. Management frames this as backed by market research that identified a demand-supply gap in quality glass beer bottles in India, and says it required enhanced manufacturing capability for high-precision, lightweight yet structurally robust containers able to withstand pressurised …

litigation.note: The only litigation-type matter visible in this bundle is a note (routed under the '=== RELATED-PARTY TRANSACTIONS ===' header, but actually a contingent-liability-style note to the standalone financial statements) stating that the Company has received GST demand notices for the period July 2017 to May 2022, against which it is in the process of filing, or has filed, appeals; management does not expect any cash outflow and no provision has been recognised. A closing line adds that future cash outflows depend on the outcome of appeals or litigations or orders and non-fulfilment of export obligation. The contingent-liability note proper, the auditor's report and the CARO annexure were NOT routed to this bundle, so no broader view of pending litigation can be formed from what was supplied.

risks.note: Management states the glass industry is energy intensive and heavily dependent on stable logistics and raw-material supply chains, and was particularly vulnerable to the FY26 disruptions; higher energy prices from supply disruptions and the new armed conflict that emerged in March 2026 are named as near-term risks to input-cost stability. Several glass manufacturers globally and some within India were compelled to curtail or temporarily suspend production.
risks.risk: Energy and fuel cost volatility in an energy-intensive process

risks.note: Price volatility in fuel and soda ash, freight disruptions and logistical constraints are explicitly listed among the challenges management had to address in advance to avoid curtailment; continuity depends on timely procurement of critical raw materials.
risks.risk: Raw-material (soda ash) price volatility and supply-chain disruption

risks.note: Management says competitive pressure due to the current surplus capacity in segments of the domestic glass industry will continue to pose challenges - a structural pricing risk for a single-segment container-glass producer.
Explicitly flagged in Risks and Concerns; the Company sells into international markets including the US and imports/ships inputs, so both translation and freight exposure sit on the margin.

US reciprocal tariffs, initially set at 26% for Indian goods and subsequently revised higher from August 2025, adversely affected Indian glass and packaging exports; management cites lingering impact of US tariff escalations and persistent uncertainty around trade-policy normalisation, though it also notes tariffs on Chinese glass have opened an opportunity.
risks.risk: Trade-policy and tariff risk on exports

risks.note: Liquor continues to account for the largest share of the Company's offtake and the business falls within a single primary segment (glass bottles / containers), so demand or regulatory shocks in alcobev pass through directly; diversification into beer, food, pharma, softdrinks and toiletries is the stated mitigation.

The MD&A's own market view notes the India glass packaging market grows at only ~4.3% CAGR through 2030 'inspite of reuse of bottles by customers and substitution by other packing alternatives in low value brands' - a structural volume drag.
risks.risk: Product substitution and bottle reuse in low-value brands

risks.note: The Board's risk-management disclosure names the common risks inter alia as regulatory risk, competition, financial risk, technology obsolescence, human resources risk, political risks, investments, retention of talent, expansion of facilities and product price risk, managed under a Risk Management Policy.
risks.risk: Technology obsolescence, talent retention and execution risk on expansion
